title: Sampling-Free Privacy Accounting for Matrix Mechanisms under Random Allocation
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: The structured matrices induce Gram matrices that are cyclically banded or decay rapidly off-diagonal, rather than strictly banded.
layout: 4 panels in a row, (a)-(d) labeled, shared diagonal heatmap structure
description: A single row of four square heatmaps, each showing a Gram matrix G on a dark-to-bright inferno-style colormap. Captions beneath read (a) BandMF p=64, (b) BSR p=64, (c) BISR p=64, (d) BandInvMF p=4. In every panel a bright diagonal runs from top-left to bottom-right. Panel (a) shows a broad orange-purple band around the diagonal on a black background. Small bright patches sit in the top-right and bottom-left corners, which shows the cyclic banding. Panels (b) and (c) are much dimmer, with a thin purple diagonal line and a faint spread around it. Panel (d) is the brightest: a yellow-white diagonal and a purple-blue background that fades smoothly away from the diagonal. The eye goes first to the bright diagonal in (d) and the corner patches in (a). There are no axes, colorbars or arrows.
caption: The Gram matrix G for matrices of size N = 3000 with k = 10. For banded matrices C, we consider Banded Matrix Factorization (BandMF) [30] and Banded Square Root Factorization (BSR) [23] with bandwidth p = 64. For banded inverse matrices, we consider Banded Inverse Matrix Factorization (BandInvMF) and Banded Inverse Square Root (BISR) [24] with bandwidths p = 4 and p = 64 accordingly. We note that although the matrix C is banded, the matrix G is not; rather, it is cyclically banded, with the corner blocks filled by strictly positive entries. Moreover, we observe that banded inverse matrices show similar behavior: their Gram matrices have entries that decay rapidly outside the cyclic band.
abstract: We study privacy amplification for differentially private model training with matrix factorization under random allocation (also known as the balls-in-bins model). Recent work by Choquette-Choo et al. (2025) proposes a sampling-based Monte Carlo approach to compute amplification parameters in this setting. However, their guarantees either only hold with some high probability or require random abstention by the mechanism. Furthermore, the required number of samples for ensuring $(Îµ,Î´)$-DP is inversely proportional to $Î´$. In contrast, we develop sampling-free bounds based on RÃ©nyi divergence and conditional composition. The former is facilitated by a dynamic programming formulation to efficiently compute the bounds. The latter complements it by offering stronger privacy guarantees for small $Îµ$, where RÃ©nyi divergence bounds inherently lead to an over-approximation. Our framework applies to arbitrary banded and non-banded matrices. Through numerical comparisons, we demonstrate the efficacy of our approach across a broad range of matrix mechanisms used in research and practice.
